statement: E1 and the opening circuit: f(u,v) is v when u=0 and is undefined when u=1. The two stored gates d=not u and b=v realise exactly this partial function; truthful transcripts on 00 and 11 are 10 and 01.
why_needed: Defines the small partial function and an actual circuit with two stored gates, so subsequent local tests apply to a complete input.

theorem exposition_toy_circuit :
  let f : QuarticQuery.PartialBool (Fin 2) := fun z =>
    if z 0 then none else some (z 1)
  let C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (Fin 2) :=
    { size := 2
      gate := fun g =>
        { left := some (.inl (if g.val = 0 then 0 else 1))
          right := none
          table := fun a _ => if g.val = 0 then !a else a }
      domainOut := 0
      valueOut := 1 }
  QuarticQuery.CircuitRealises C f ∧
    ∀ z : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2),

statement: The complete four-column board in Section 1 has X=(1111,0111,1011,1101), two address inputs 11 in column 2 and 00 elsewhere, and the displayed outgoing row targets and truthful transcripts repeated in every cell. It has 192 physical bits (E2), 15 local tests (E4), and exactly one winner, at column 1/address00. The winning pointers land on X2[1]=X3[2]=X4[3]=0 (E3). At addresses 00,01,10,11 the failure counts are respectively (0,1,1,2), (7,6,6,5), (3,4,4,5), (3,4,4,5) by column; hence the proposed-address counts are 0,5,3,3.
why_needed: Makes the entire pedagogical input and its displayed tables a finite statement rather than treating a nearby general theorem as proof of these data.
proposed_lean:
theorem exposition_toy_board :
  let f : QuarticQuery.PartialBool (Fin 2) := fun z =>
    if z 0 then none else some (z 1)
  let C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (Fin 2) :=
    { size := 2
      gate := fun g =>
        { left := some (.inl (if g.val = 0 then 0 else 1))
          right := none
          table := fun a _ => if g.val = 0 then !a else a }
      domainOut := 0
      valueOut := 1 }
  let target : QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Column 2 :=
    fun i j =>
      if i.val = 0 then (if j.val = 1 then 0 else if j.val = 2 then 1 else 2)
      else if i.val = 1 then (if j.val = 2 then 1 else 0)
      else if i.val = 2 then (if j.val = 3 then 2 else if j.val = 1 then 1 else 0)
      else 0
  let x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.BitLoc 2 2 2 (Fin 2)) := fun q =>
    match q with
    | .inl (i, j) => if i.val = 0 then true else decide (j.val ≠ i.val - 1)
    | .inr (.inl (i, _, _)) => decide (i.val = 1)
    | .inr (.inr (.inl ⟨i, (_, j, b)⟩)) =>
        (QuarticQuery.pointerEquiv 2).symm (target i j.val) b
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (i, _, _, g))) =>
        if g.val = 0 then decide (i.val ≠ 1) else decide (i.val = 1)
  let s0 : QuarticQuery.Address 2 := fun _ => false
  QuarticQuery.CircuitRealises C f ∧
    Fintype.card (QuarticQuery.BitLoc 2 2 2 (Fin 2)) = 192 ∧
    Fintype.card (QuarticQuery.TestIndex 2 2 2) = 15 ∧
    (∀ i s, QuarticQuery.WinsAt f C 2 2 x i s ↔ i = 0 ∧ s = s0) ∧
    (∀ (i : QuarticQuery.Column 2) (s : QuarticQuery.Address 2),
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun q : QuarticQuery.TestIndex 2 2 2 =>
        QuarticQuery.localTest C 2 2 x i s q = false)).card =
      if i.val = 0 then (Finset.univ.filter (fun h : Fin 2 => s h = true)).card
      else if i.val = 1 then 7 - (Finset.univ.filter (fun h : Fin 2 => s h = true)).card
      else 3 + (Finset.univ.filter (fun h : Fin 2 => s h = true)).card)

statement: With row codebook 1->00, 2->01, 3->10, 4->11 and pointers ordered by destination column followed by two (d,b) transcripts, the four repeated cell words are 0001101010, 0001000101, 0001101010, 0000001010. Every word has length10.

theorem exposition_printed_cell_words :
  let code : Fin 4 → List Bool := fun j =>
    if j.val = 0 then [false, false]
    else if j.val = 1 then [false, true]
    else if j.val = 2 then [true, false] else [true, true]
  let targets : Fin 4 → List (Fin 4) := fun i =>
    if i.val = 0 then [0, 1, 2]
    else if i.val = 1 then [0, 1, 0]
    else if i.val = 2 then [0, 1, 2] else [0, 0, 0]
  let transcript : Fin 4 → List Bool := fun i =>
    if i.val = 1 then [false, true] else [true, false]
  let cell : Fin 4 → List Bool := fun i =>
    (targets i).flatMap code ++ transcript i ++ transcript i
  cell 0 = [false, false, false, true, true, false, true, false, true, false] ∧
    cell 1 = [false, false, false, true, false, false, false, true, false, true] ∧
    cell 2 = [false, false, false, true, true, false, true, false, true, false] ∧
    cell 3 = [false, false, false, false, false, false, true, false, true, false] ∧
    ∀ i, (cell i).length = 10

statement: On the full toy input, proposing the v-bit address and choosing the sole disqualifier or smaller index produces the exact matrix E5: [[0,1,1,1],[0,0,1,0],[0,0,0,1],[0,1,0,0]]. Thus 2 beats3, 3 beats4, 4 beats2, and1 beats every opponent, including the undefined-address column2.

theorem exposition_toy_comparison :
  let f : QuarticQuery.PartialBool (Fin 2) := fun z =>
    if z 0 then none else some (z 1)
  let C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (Fin 2) :=
    { size := 2
      gate := fun g =>
        { left := some (.inl (if g.val = 0 then 0 else 1))
          right := none
          table := fun a _ => if g.val = 0 then !a else a }
      domainOut := 0
      valueOut := 1 }
  let target : QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Column 2 :=
    fun i j =>
      if i.val = 0 then (if j.val = 1 then 0 else if j.val = 2 then 1 else 2)
      else if i.val = 1 then (if j.val = 2 then 1 else 0)
      else if i.val = 2 then (if j.val = 3 then 2 else if j.val = 1 then 1 else 0)
      else 0
  let x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.BitLoc 2 2 2 (Fin 2)) := fun q =>
    match q with
    | .inl (i, j) => if i.val = 0 then true else decide (j.val ≠ i.val - 1)
    | .inr (.inl (i, _, _)) => decide (i.val = 1)
    | .inr (.inr (.inl ⟨i, (_, j, b)⟩)) =>
        (QuarticQuery.pointerEquiv 2).symm (target i j.val) b
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (i, _, _, g))) =>
        if g.val = 0 then decide (i.val ≠ 1) else decide (i.val = 1)
  let s0 : QuarticQuery.Address 2 := fun _ => false
  let guess : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.BitLoc 2 2 2 (Fin 2)) →
      QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Address 2 := fun y i h =>
    QuarticQuery.readA y i h (1 : Fin 2)
  let disqualifies : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.BitLoc 2 2 2 (Fin 2)) →
      QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Column 2 → Bool := fun y i j =>
    if h : j ≠ i then
      !(QuarticQuery.readX y j (QuarticQuery.pointerEquiv 2
        (QuarticQuery.readPointerBit y i (guess y i) ⟨j, h⟩)))
    else false
  let cmp : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.BitLoc 2 2 2 (Fin 2)) →
      QuarticQuery.Column 2 → QuarticQuery.Column 2 → Bool := fun y i j =>
    if i = j then false
    else if disqualifies y i j = disqualifies y j i then decide (i.val < j.val)
    else disqualifies y i j
  ∀ i j : QuarticQuery.Column 2, cmp x i j = decide
    (i ≠ j ∧ (i.val = 0 ∨
      (i.val = 1 ∧ j.val = 2) ∨ (i.val = 2 ∧ j.val = 3) ∨
      (i.val = 3 ∧ j.val = 1)))

theorem exposition_cyclic_dynamics :
  let a : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → ℝ := fun i j =>
    if i ≠ j ∧ (i.val = 0 ∨
      (i.val = 1 ∧ j.val = 2) ∨ (i.val = 2 ∧ j.val = 3) ∨
      (i.val = 3 ∧ j.val = 1)) then 1 else 0
  QuarticQuery.Tournament.IsComparison a ∧
    QuarticQuery.Tournament.UnitValued a ∧
    (∀ p i : Fin 4, QuarticQuery.Tournament.weight a [p] i = a i p) ∧
    (∀ p : Fin 4,
      QuarticQuery.Tournament.total (QuarticQuery.Tournament.weight a [p]) =
        if p = 0 then 0 else 2) ∧
    QuarticQuery.Tournament.expectAfter a 1
      (fun w _ => QuarticQuery.Tournament.total w) = 3 / 2 ∧
    QuarticQuery.Tournament.prob a 1 (fun _ L => (0 : Fin 4) ∉ L) = 3 / 4 ∧
    QuarticQuery.Tournament.prob a 2 (fun _ L => (0 : Fin 4) ∉ L) = 3 / 8 ∧
    QuarticQuery.Tournament.prob a 3 (fun _ L => (0 : Fin 4) ∉ L) = 0 ∧

    QuarticQuery.Tournament.expectAfter a 3

    (∀ i : Fin 4, w i / QuarticQuery.Tournament.total w =
      if i = 0 then 1 / 2 else if i = 1 then 0 else 1 / 4) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin 4, z i = if i = 0 then 1 else if i = 3 then 1 / 4 else 0) ∧
    z 0 / QuarticQuery.Tournament.total z = 4 / 5 ∧

    QuarticQuery.Tournament.prob a 1 (fun _ L => (0 : Fin 4) ∉ L) = 3 / 4 ∧

statement: For uniform two-bit AND the one-query optimum is3/4. The early-stopping exact tree has depth2, uses one query on inputs00,01 only, and has Pr(E)=Pr(E and correct)=1/2 and Pr(correct|E)=1 (E11). Aborting before the second query and answering0 has success3/4. For two independent copies the original joint cap event has probability1/4; the optimal all-correct probability under separate one-query caps is9/16, even with adaptive interleaving.
why_needed: Makes the conditioning pitfall and the corrected simulator argument exact.

theorem exposition_AND_conditioning :
  let f : QuarticQuery.PartialBool (Fin 2) := QuarticQuery.totalise (fun z => z 0 && z 1)
  let mu : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2) → ℝ := fun _ => 1 / 4
  let T : QuarticQuery.QueryTree (Fin 2) :=
    .query 0 (.leaf false) (.query 1 (.leaf false) (.leaf true))
  let capped : QuarticQuery.QueryTree (Fin 2) := .query 0 (.leaf false) (.leaf false)
  let used : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2) → ℕ := fun z => if z 0 then 2 else 1
  let event : ℝ := ∑ z : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2),
    if used z ≤ 1 then mu z else 0
  let joint : ℝ := ∑ z : QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2),
    if used z ≤ 1 ∧ f z = some (T.eval z) then mu z else 0
  QuarticQuery.budgetValue f 1 mu = 3 / 4 ∧
    (∀ z, f z = some (T.eval z)) ∧ T.depth = 2 ∧ capped.depth = 1 ∧
    event = 1 / 2 ∧ joint = 1 / 2 ∧ joint / event = 1 ∧
    QuarticQuery.treeSuccess f mu capped = 3 / 4 ∧
    (1 / 2 : ℝ)^2 = 1 / 4 ∧ (3 / 4 : ℝ)^2 = 9 / 16 ∧
    (∀ U : QuarticQuery.OutTree (Fin 2 × Fin 2) (Fin 2 → Bool),
      U.capped (fun _ => 1) →
        QuarticQuery.guessSuccess f (fun _ => mu) U ≤ 9 / 16) ∧
    QuarticQuery.guessSuccess f (fun _ => mu)
      (QuarticQuery.OutTree.leaf (fun _ : Fin 2 => false)) = 9 / 16 ∧
    (∑ U : Fin 2 → QuarticQuery.BitInput (Fin 2),
      if (∀ h, used (U h) ≤ 1) then (1 / 16 : ℝ) else 0) = 1 / 4

      domainOut := 0
      valueOut := 1 }

    if i.val = 0 then 3 else if i.val = 1 then 0 else if i.val = 2 then 1 else 2

theorem exposition_forrelation_three_inputs :
  let zp : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord 2 1) :=
    fun q => decide (q.2.val = 3)
  let zz : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord 2 1) :=
    fun q => if q.1.val = 0 then decide (q.2.val = 2) else decide (q.2.val = 3)
  let zm : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord 2 1) :=
    fun q => if q.1.val = 0 then decide (q.2.val ≠ 3) else decide (q.2.val = 3)
  QuarticQuery.forrelationDenominator 2 1 = 8 ∧
    QuarticQuery.forrelationNumerator 2 1 zp = 8 ∧
    QuarticQuery.forrelationNumerator 2 1 zz = 0 ∧
    QuarticQuery.forrelationNumerator 2 1 zm = -8 ∧
    QuarticQuery.Phi 2 1 zp = 1 ∧ QuarticQuery.Phi 2 1 zz = 0 ∧ QuarticQuery.Phi 2 1 zm = -1 ∧
    QuarticQuery.P 2 1 zp = some true ∧ QuarticQuery.P 2 1 zz = some false ∧
    QuarticQuery.P 2 1 zm = none
